back: A line through a plotted point extending one absolute uncertainty either side of it, showing the range in which the true value lies.
The steepest or shallowest straight line that still passes through every error bar.
notes: Uncertainty in gradient = |best gradient − worst gradient|.

back: $\lg y = n\lg x + \lg a$: plot $\lg y$ against $\lg x$; gradient $n$, intercept $\lg a$.
$\ln y = kx + \ln a$: plot $\ln y$ against $x$; gradient $k$, intercept $\ln a$.

front: Uncertainty in $\ln y$ and in $\lg y$?
back: $\Delta(\ln y) \approx \Delta y / y$; $\Delta(\lg y) \approx 0.434\,\Delta y / y$ (or half of $\lg(y+\Delta y) - \lg(y-\Delta y)$).

front: How many decimal places for a logarithm in a table?
back: As many decimal places as the raw reading has significant figures (or one more).

front: How should a column of logarithms be headed?
back: With the unit inside the bracket, e.g. $\lg(d/\text{mm})$ or $\ln(V/\text{V})$; a logarithm has no unit.

front: How do you find the y-intercept when the graph has a false origin?
back: Calculate it: $c = y - mx$, using a point on the line and the gradient.

front: How is a constant found from a gradient quoted?
back: As value ± absolute uncertainty with a unit, e.g. $k = (1.00 \pm 0.04) \times 10^{-2}\ \text{s}^{-1}$; percentage uncertainties of quantities multiplied together add.
